claims.statement: The supplied action-specific record supports a general technical-enablement direction for HTTPS/TLS by reporting that a 2024 session-hijacking study treats encrypted web communication and related secure-session practices as concrete countermeasures against interception-oriented hijacking and supports HTTPS/TLS as an important transport-layer control within a broader session-protection strategy.

The supplied action-specific record provides a general technical-limitation direction by reporting that session tokens can still be stolen through XSS or malicious browser extensions after a secure transport channel exists and that HTTPS alone cannot cover all session-hijacking paths, including scenarios in which existing session protections are ineffective against user-level malware.

The supplied SSL VPN case study is eligible only as deployment_maturity context: it describes planning, design, and prototype implementation of an SSL VPN solution using commonly available equipment and software, but it does not by itself establish a directional feasibility conclusion for HTTPS under the grounding contract.

conditional_requirements: A DEPLOYMENT_SPECIFIC technical feasibility conclusion would require exact supplied evidence on local network/application architecture and whether the environment can support the HTTPS/TLS session protections under evaluation.

A sufficiency conclusion for session-hijacking mitigation would require supplied evidence on residual token-theft paths in the local environment and the availability of complementary session controls, without assuming exact products, versions, or vendors.
constraints: HTTPS/TLS is supported as a transport-layer control within a broader session-protection strategy, not as a complete solution for every session-hijacking path.
The challenge evidence limits the threat-mitigation fit of HTTPS alone where session tokens can be exposed after transport encryption, such as through XSS or malicious browser extensions.

No deployment-specific compatibility conclusion can be drawn from the supplied records because the frozen infrastructure context does not report local architecture, TLS termination points, application session-management design, certificate infrastructure, or client/browser environment.
evidence_gaps: No supplied record establishes whether HTTPS has been deployed, enforced, or operationally effective in the frozen enterprise by the cutoff or within the 2025-2027 horizon.
No supplied record provides post-cutoff session-hijacking exploitation signal or effectiveness measurements for HTTPS against the frozen threat.
The region is masked and no jurisdiction-specific technical evidence is supplied, so no region-driven technical feasibility direction can be inferred.
assessment.rationale: The grounded general technical_enablement record supports HTTPS/TLS as a relevant transport-layer countermeasure for interception-oriented session hijacking, while the grounded general technical_limitation record shows that HTTPS alone does not cover all session-hijacking paths. The eligible deployment_maturity record supplies only non-directional implementation context. Because the frozen infrastructure context does not report exact local architecture or operational-effectiveness detail, the technical feasibility direction remains mixed at GENERAL scope rather than decisively supported or challenged.

equivalence_key: Multi-department enterprise IT with personnel responsible for managing and protecting infrastructure; the environment may require enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise for some safeguards.

No numeric budget, price, ROI, TCO, staffing count, or procurement ceiling is assumed. Resource capacity is represented only by the frozen CIS IG2 reference profile; exact financial quantities remain unknown.
